title: Immersive generating sections under module isomorphism and finite reindexing
statement: Let X and B be schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and f:X→B a morphism. Let I,J be finite index types with an equivalence e:J≃I, and let M,N be invertible O_X-modules [def-sc-invertible-module] with an isomorphism α:M≅N. Suppose finite global-section families s:I→Γ(X,M) and t:J→Γ(X,N) satisfy α(s(e(j)))=t(j) for every j. If s generates M [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections] and its associated morphism X→P(I;B) [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections] is an immersion [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], then t generates N and its associated morphism X→P(J;B) is an immersion. No smoothness, dimension, field, prescribed-point, compactification, or existence assumption is involved.

proof.text: Use generating_sections_iff_stalk_span to reindex the generating family: the range of its germs is unchanged because e is surjective. Under the section-preserving isomorphism alpha, the new evaluation map is the reindexed old evaluation map followed by alpha.hom (freeHomEquiv_symm_comp). It is therefore epi, including for empty coordinate types.

Use integralHomOfGeneratingSections_spec for the old generating family over Spec Z and the adjunction-uniqueness comparison from tensor pullback to ordinary module pullback to obtain its universal pair. The preimages of the standard opens cover X, and the pulled-back coordinate sections give free generators there. The module isomorphism alpha carries those restricted generators to the corresponding new sections. Identify the native homOfIsFreeGenerator morphism for each family with homOfGeneratingSections: the native twistRestrictHom gives its universal pair, adjunction uniqueness identifies ordinary and tensor pullback, and the integral classification plus the two projective-space projections proves equality over the arbitrary base B.

Use the existing isIso_homOfIsFreeGenerator_reindex construction for the coordinate permutation R:P(I;B)→P(J;B). On the chart indexed by j it pulls T_l/T_j back to T_(e l)/T_(e j). Compare the old native morphism followed by R with the new native morphism on the reindexed cover. The section-ratio equations agree after applying alpha, by its O_X-linearity and naturality. Equality on a chart over arbitrary B follows by composing both maps with projective-space base change to Spec Z, applying affine-base chart-ratio extensionality there, and then comparing the two projections to B and the integral Proj. Glue the chart equalities.

Rewrite the new classified morphism as the old classified morphism followed by the isomorphism R. The composition of an immersion with an isomorphism is an immersion. The cover argument is valid for the empty cover as well, so no nonemptiness hypothesis or separate exceptional case is needed.

theorem generatingSections_immersion_iso_reindex
    {X B : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ B)
    {I J : Type u} [Finite I] [Finite J] (e : J ≃ I)
    (M N : X.Modules) [M.IsInvertible] [N.IsInvertible] (α : M ≅ N)
    (s : I → Γ(M, ⊤)) (t : J → Γ(N, ⊤))
    (ht : ∀ j, α.hom.app ⊤ (s (e j)) = t j)
    (hs : ∃ h : Epi (M.freeHomEquiv.symm
        (fun i ↦ SheafOfModules.unitHomEquiv _ (homOfGlobalSection M (s i)))),
      IsImmersion (@homOfGeneratingSections I inferInstance X B f M inferInstance
        (fun i ↦ SheafOfModules.unitHomEquiv _ (homOfGlobalSection M (s i))) h)) :
    ∃ h : Epi (N.freeHomEquiv.symm
        (fun j ↦ SheafOfModules.unitHomEquiv _ (homOfGlobalSection N (t j)))),
      IsImmersion (@homOfGeneratingSections J inferInstance X B f N inferInstance
        (fun j ↦ SheafOfModules.unitHomEquiv _ (homOfGlobalSection N (t j))) h)
